17592186087689.knowledge-point/title: Finding Exact Solutions to Exponential Equations Using the Natural Logarithm

17592186087494.question/problem: What is the value of $x$ if $e^{x - 3}=2^5?$
17592186087494.question/worked-solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $\left(\ln\right)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x-3} & ={2}^{5} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{x-3}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{5})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\ln \left( e^a \right) = a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

$$
x-3 = \ln \left( 2^5 \right).
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$ and rewrite the right-hand side using the power law of logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-3 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{5}) \\ x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{5})+3 \\ x & =5\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=5\ln (2) + 3.$

17592186233027.question/problem: Find the exact solution of the equation ${e}^{t}=11.$
17592186233027.question/worked-solution:
First, we find the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & =11 \\ \operatorname{ln}({e}^{t}) & =\operatorname{ln}(11)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
t=\operatorname{ln}(11)
$$

Therefore, the solution is $t=\operatorname{ln}(11).$

17592186234220.question/problem: What is the value of $x$ if ${e}^{2x+3}=\sqrt[5]{7}?$
17592186234220.question/worked-solution:
First, we find the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{2x+3} & =\sqrt[5]{7} \\ \operatorname{ln}({e}^{2x+3}) & =\operatorname{ln}(\sqrt[5]{7})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
2x+3=\operatorname{ln}(\sqrt[5]{7})
$$

Next, we write $\sqrt[5]{7}$ as ${7}^{1/5}.$ So, we get:

$$
2x+3=\operatorname{ln}({7}^{1/5})
$$

Finally, we rewrite the right-hand side using power law of logarithms and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+3 & =\operatorname{ln}({7}^{1/5}) \\ 2x+3 & =\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{ln}(7) \\ 2x & =\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{ln}(7)-3 \\ x & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{ln}(7)-3) \\ x & =\frac{1}{10}\operatorname{ln}7-\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=\frac{1}{10}\operatorname{ln}7-\frac{3}{2}.$

17592186546961.question/problem: What is the value of $y$ if ${e}^{7-y}=\sqrt[7]{10}?$
17592186546961.question/worked-solution:
First, we find the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{7-y} & =\sqrt[7]{10} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{7-y}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt[7]{10})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
7-y=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt[7]{10})
$$

Next, we write $\sqrt[7]{10}$ as ${10}^{1/7}.$ So, we get:

$$
7-y=\operatorname{ln}⁡({10}^{1/7})
$$

Finally, we rewrite the right-hand side using power law of logarithms and solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}7-y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({10}^{1/7}) \\ 7-y & =\frac{1}{7}\operatorname{ln}⁡(10) \\ -y & =\frac{1}{7}\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)-7 \\ y & =7-\frac{1}{7}\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $y=7-\frac{1}{7}\operatorname{ln}⁡(10).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{5-y} & =\sqrt[4]{7} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{5-y}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt[4]{7})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
5-y=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt[4]{7})
$$

Next, we write $\sqrt[4]{7}$ as ${7}^{1/4}.$ So, we get:

$$
5-y=\operatorname{ln}⁡({7}^{1/4})
$$

Finally, we rewrite the right-hand side using power law of logarithms and solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$

Therefore, the solution is $y=5-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(7).$

17592186601933.question/worked-solution:
First, we find the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{4-5y} & =21 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{4-5y}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(21)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

$$
4-5y=\operatorname{ln}⁡(21).
$$

Finally, we solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4-5y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(21) \\ -5y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(21)-4 \\ y & =-\frac{1}{5}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(21)-4) \\ y & =\frac{4}{5}-\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡(21)\end{aligned}

Therefore, the solution is $y=\frac{4}{5}-\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡(21).$

17592186655623.question/worked-solution:
First, we find the natural logarithm $(\ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}e^{-3y-7}&=24 \\ \ln(e^{-3y-7})&=\ln(24)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\ln(e^u)=u$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

$$
-3y-7=\ln(24).
$$

Finally, we solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3y-7&=\ln(24) \\ -3y&=\ln(24)+7 \\ y&=\frac{1}{-3}\left(\ln(24)+7\right) \\ y&=-\frac{7}{3}-\frac{1}{3}\ln(24)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $y=-\frac{7}{3}-\frac{1}{3}\ln(24).$

17592186655624.question/worked-solution:
First, we find the natural logarithm $(\ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}e^{4+4y}&=25 \\ \ln(e^{4+4y})&=\ln(25)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\ln(e^u)=u$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

$$
4+4y=\ln(25).
$$

Finally, we solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4+4y&=\ln(25) \\ 4y&=\ln(25)-4 \\ y&=\frac{1}{4}\left(\ln(25)-4\right) \\ y&=-1+\frac{1}{4}\ln(25)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $y=-1+\frac{1}{4}\ln(25).$

17592186655625.question/worked-solution:

Therefore, the solution is $y=-\frac{3}{2}+\frac{1}{2}\ln(10).$

17592186670922.question/problem: What is the exact value of $t$ if $e^{6+2t}=\sqrt[6]{13}$?
17592186670922.question/worked-solution:
Take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\ln\left(e^{6+2t}\right)&=\ln\left(\sqrt[6]{13}\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Use $\ln(e^u)=u$ and write the root as a fractional power:

$$
\begin{aligned}6+2t&=\ln\left(13^{1/6}\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the power rule for logarithms:

$$
\begin{aligned}6+2t&=\frac{1}{6}\ln\left(13\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Subtract the constant term, then divide by the signed coefficient of $t$:

$$
\begin{aligned}2t&=\frac{1}{6}\ln\left(13\right)-6 \\ t&=-3+\frac{1}{12}\ln\left(13\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $t=-3+\frac{1}{12}\ln\left(13\right)$.

17592186670923.question/problem: What is the exact value of $x$ if $e^{2+3x}=\sqrt[4]{3}$?
17592186670923.question/worked-solution:
Take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\ln\left(e^{2+3x}\right)&=\ln\left(\sqrt[4]{3}\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Use $\ln(e^u)=u$ and write the root as a fractional power:

$$
\begin{aligned}2+3x&=\ln\left(3^{1/4}\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the power rule for logarithms:

$$
\begin{aligned}2+3x&=\frac{1}{4}\ln\left(3\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Subtract the constant term, then divide by the signed coefficient of $x$:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x&=\frac{1}{4}\ln\left(3\right)-2 \\ x&=-\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{12}\ln\left(3\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x=-\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{12}\ln\left(3\right)$.

17592186670924.question/problem: What is the exact value of $y$ if $e^{-2y+4}=\sqrt[8]{7}$?
17592186670924.question/worked-solution:
Take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\ln\left(e^{-2y+4}\right)&=\ln\left(\sqrt[8]{7}\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Use $\ln(e^u)=u$ and write the root as a fractional power:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2y+4&=\ln\left(7^{1/8}\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the power rule for logarithms:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2y+4&=\frac{1}{8}\ln\left(7\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Subtract the constant term, then divide by the signed coefficient of $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2y&=\frac{1}{8}\ln\left(7\right)-4 \\ y&=2-\frac{1}{16}\ln\left(7\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $y=2-\frac{1}{16}\ln\left(7\right)$.
